column3: The Hebrew repeats Philistines and has no separate many.
The Hebrew repeats Philistines as the subject of killing; BSB uses they.
The Hebrew says the archers found him and he was wounded; BSB says they overtook him and wounded him.
The Hebrew says the sword without an ownership expression; BSB says his own sword.
The Hebrew says the sword without an ownership expression; BSB says his own sword.
The Hebrew repeats the verb die; BSB expresses it once.
The Hebrew says they had fled without explicitly naming an army; BSB supplies the army.
The Hebrew says they carried away his head and equipment, without an explicit cutting verb, messengers, or temple; BSB supplies these details.
The Hebrew explicitly names his skull and uses a fastening verb; BSB says his head and hung.
The Hebrew says all Jabesh-gilead; BSB supplies the people.
The Hebrew distinguishes Saul’s singular body from the plural bodies of his sons; BSB combines both in bodies.
The Hebrew repeats the unfaithfulness root as noun and verb; BSB expresses it once.
The Hebrew continues with an unexpressed subject for put him to death; BSB names the LORD again.
